newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian CPI up 0.06 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian CPI up 0.06 pct in October.

text.p: The Palestinian consumer price index (CPI) in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and Arab East Jerusalem rose 0.06 percent in October, the Palestinian Central Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday.

This follows a 0.31 increase in September. The Statistics Bureau said in a statement the CPI rise brought annual inflation to 8.27 percent between November 1995 -- when the department began calculating the index -- and October 1996.
Prices rose in most main sectors, led by sharp increases in education and transportation, but a 1.18 percent drop in October food prices kept the CPI low.
Traders blamed an Israeli closure barring Palestinian exports and blocking trade between West Bank and Gaza self-rule enclaves for the drop in food prices.
"During October, prices of fruits vegetables marked a reduction because they were exposed to decay and were banned entry to the West Bank," Gazan wholesaler Maher Ahmad told Reuters.
Israel, citing security reasons, periodically seals off the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
The Statistics Bureau said consumer prices rose by 0.70 percent in East Jerusalem and 0.15 percent in the West Bank during the month but that prices fell by 0.64 percent in the Gaza Strip.
